title: Sail and rigging plan of the U.S.S. Polaris
creator: U.S. Navy draughtsman
description: The sail and rigging plan of the Polaris as fitted out for the North Polar Expedition of 1871: masts, spars and standing rigging drawn to scale. She began as the steam tug America, was rebuilt for the ice, carried Charles Francis Hall to Thank God Harbor, and was wrecked at Etah in 1872.

title: Deck plans of the U.S.S. Polaris
creator: U.S. Navy draughtsman
description: The upper and lower deck plans of the Polaris, showing the cabins, the hold, the boilers and the stowage - how nineteen men and their two Inuit families were fitted into a rebuilt tug of 387 tons.

title: The brig Advance nipped off Cape Cornelius Grinnell, Melville Bay
creator: after a sketch by Elisha Kent Kane
description: The Advance caught between closing floes in Melville Bay in 1853, from Kane's own sketch. The brig had already carried the first Grinnell expedition of 1850-51; she was abandoned at Rensselaer Harbor in May 1855 and never recovered.
